nodes.statement:
Institutional excerpt for review: Dog bites and scratches cause 99% of the human rabies cases and can be prevented through dog vaccination and bite prevention.

However, rabies deaths are preventable with prompt post exposure prophylaxis (PEP) by stopping the virus from reaching the central nervous system. PEP consists of thorough wound washing, administration of a course of human rabies vaccine and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulins (RIG) or monoclonal antibodies (RmAb).

WHO and its global partners aim to end human deaths from dog-mediated rabies through a comprehensive One Health approach promoting mass dog vaccination, ensuring access to PEP, health worker training, improved surveillance, and bite prevention through community awareness.

Vaccinating dogs, including puppies, through mass dog vaccination programs is the most cost-effective strategy for preventing rabies in people because it stops the transmission at its source.

provenance.source_scope: WHO global rabies fact sheet; not local service coverage data
provenance.boundary: Source text was supplied; source content authentication is separate from this packet.

nodes.statement:
Institutional excerpt for review: DPM supports effective and sustainable rabies control programmes and the control of other zoonoses. Recognising that mass culling of dogs is ineffective and may be counterproductive, reducing dog population size is not an effective means of reducing rabies prevalence . However, DPM can contribute to rabies control by reducing population turnover, therefore supporting maintenance of herd immunity within a vaccinated dog population. The components of population turnover most relevant for rabies control are the reduction in the birth of puppies that would be at risk of remaining unvaccinated and the improvement of welfare and life expectancy of vaccinated dogs.

Development of DPM programmes should include an initial assessment and ongoing adaptation based on continued monitoring and evaluation using objective methods. This evidence-based approach improves programme effectiveness and informs responses to changes in the wider context that influence dog population dynamics.

Estimation of dog population size and demography. Dog population size estimates can help with planning DPM programm

provenance.source_scope: WOAH 2024 Terrestrial Code chapter 7.7; normative recommendations, not observed local outcomes
provenance.boundary: Source text was supplied; source content authentication is separate from this packet.

nodes.statement: Institutional excerpt for review: Seven [ 33 , 36 , 44 – 46 , 51 , 53 ] of the eight studies analyzed in this group used census surveys to estimate the size of the free-ranging dog populations. These studies reported the simple counting of the dogs viewed or photographed during a given period of time, and this value was computed as the population abundance. This approach does not take into account the possibility of heterogeneous probabilities of animal detection and can only generate indicators of canine abundance instead of estimates of population parameters of abundance [ 22 ].

provenance.source_scope: 2015 systematic methodological review, 26 studies; not a 2026 dog population census
provenance.boundary: Source text was supplied; source content authentication is separate from this packet.

nodes.statement: Simple counts of free-ranging dogs observed or photographed may be indicators rather than population-parameter abundance estimates when heterogeneous detection probability is not addressed.

provenance.scope: Belo et al. 2015 systematic-methods review, census method subset
provenance.limitation: Does not establish that every count is unusable or estimate the magnitude of bias at any current site.

quote_receipts.quote: This approach does not take into account the possibility of heterogeneous probabilities of animal detection and can only generate indicators of canine abundance instead of estimates of population parameters of abundance

provenance.second_pass_rationale: Source supports limitations of reviewed simple-count approaches, not all population surveys.
provenance.boundary: Quotation matches source excerpt; proposition not independently checked for entailment.

nodes.statement: WOAH says trends in free-roaming dog density and reproduction may sometimes suffice for DPM evaluation without repeated total-population estimates.

provenance.reason: Detection-biased raw sighting counts cannot automatically be interpreted as a valid planning denominator, even when dog population estimates would be useful to a DPM program.
provenance.limitations: Site-specific sampling, detection correction, population definition and uncertainty remain to be measured.
provenance.second_pass_rationale: Bias can qualify planning estimates, but denominator validity needs local testing.
provenance.boundary: LLM-proposed association between two atomized statements. Sources have not been independently checked for the relationship.

provenance.reason: The WOAH planning requirement for dog population estimates and coverage informs how to interpret WHO vaccination-program ambitions.
provenance.limitations: Population estimates do not demonstrate delivered vaccine doses, immunization coverage or rabies outcomes.
provenance.second_pass_rationale: Population estimation and vaccine strategy share coverage concerns, but no campaign performance measured.
provenance.boundary: LLM-proposed association between two atomized statements. Sources have not been independently checked for the relationship.

provenance.reason: WOAH's dog-turnover mechanism provides a dynamic constraint on sustained herd immunity, complementing WHO's mass dog vaccination strategy.
provenance.limitations: Local births, movement, dog immunity, vaccination uptake and mortality trends are absent.
provenance.second_pass_rationale: Turnover creates an immunity-maintenance issue; local vaccination cohorts not observed.
provenance.boundary: LLM-proposed association between two atomized statements. Sources have not been independently checked for the relationship.

provenance.reason: WOAH's rejection of dog-culling as a rabies-control substitute differentiates reducing visible dog numbers from WHO's dog vaccination strategy.
provenance.limitations: This is a cross-source program-logic comparison, not a controlled local efficacy evaluation.
provenance.second_pass_rationale: Normative guidance differentiates culling and vaccination without a local comparative trial.
provenance.boundary: LLM-proposed association between two atomized statements. Sources have not been independently checked for the relationship.

provenance.reason: WHO treats human PEP access as part of the same prevention package as dog vaccination, with time-sensitive clinical management following exposure.
provenance.limitations: No population-level data on PEP timing, financial access or treatment completion were supplied.
provenance.second_pass_rationale: WHO treats human PEP as a complementary prevention component; actual access unmeasured.
provenance.boundary: LLM-proposed association between two atomized statements. Sources have not been independently checked for the relationship.

provenance.reason: The possibility of owned dogs roaming complicates interpretation of a simple count as a count of unowned animals and interacts with detection limitations.
provenance.limitations: Neither source quantifies ownership-specific roaming or its contribution to estimation bias in any locality.
provenance.second_pass_rationale: WOAH discusses roaming ownership whereas Belo reviews detection; combined survey bias is a hypothesis needing evidence.
provenance.boundary: LLM-proposed association between two atomized statements. Sources have not been independently checked for the relationship.

provenance.reason: WOAH's acceptable program-trend monitoring targets differ from the unbiased total-abundance estimates that the systematic review warns against conflating with raw counts.
provenance.limitations: A route-density time series still requires stable sampling conditions and cannot establish a causal program impact.
provenance.second_pass_rationale: Trend and abundance measurement differ; neither is free of sampling issues.

provenance.limitations: Local incidence, care pathway, treatment delays and patient outcomes remain unobserved.
provenance.second_pass_rationale: Exposure and PEP appear at distinct points in the human rabies prevention pathway.
